question.problem: Express the compound inequality $x < 4$ or $x \ge 10$ using interval notation.
question.worked_solution:
We can represent the compound inequality on a number line, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191664/assets/26594fb87ed7eca0803d554e4a1fbd3d3719cc01ba4e70f96126b73924ac5769.png)

This number line consists of the interval $(-\infty, 4)$ as well as the interval $[10, \infty).$

So, we can express the compound inequality as the union of these two intervals:

$$
(-\infty, 4) \:{\cup}\: [10, \infty)
$$
